best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of a season abruptly cut short. Before the pandemic shuttered theaters that spring, these productions had just begun establishing themselves, and their lasting impact continues to resonate with audiences today.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which earns an 83/100 from critics for its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This reimagined production demonstrates how classic musicals can find new relevance through bold directorial choices, though the approach doesn't win over every traditionalist.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as perhaps the most significant theatrical event of this cohort—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally received its long-overdue Broadway premiere in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race and power in the military remains urgently relevant. With a 78/100 score across 29 reviews, it represents both a historical correction and a contemporary triumph.

The season also brought notable experiments in form and interpretation. Laura Linney's solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics but showcases the actress at her most luminous, while Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining sparked passionate debate about how far classic works should be pushed in revival.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the shows that opened in 2020 reflect a Broadway willing to take risks—whether through stripped-down storytelling, long-delayed premieres, or provocative reinterpretations. For theatergoers interested in this pivotal season, these productions offer essential perspectives on where Broadway was heading before everything changed.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—the industry's triumphant return following an unprecedented 18-month pandemic shutdown. These productions, which began with Pass Over's symbolic reopening in August 2021, showcase an art form that emerged from crisis with renewed urgency and creative ambition.

The ten highest-rated shows from this pivotal year average an impressive 81/100 critical score, reflecting both the quality of work and critics' enthusiasm for theater's comeback. Leading the pack is Dana H., Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance, which critics hail as mesmerizing and unforgettable despite its challenging subject matter. Close behind, The Phantom of the Opera—which would ultimately close in 2023 after 35 years—reminds audiences why Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical became a cultural phenomenon, while Rebecca Frecknall's immersive Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club transforms the Playhouse Theatre into pre-war Berlin with widespread acclaim.

The year's offerings span remarkable range: verbatim docudrama (Is This a Room), epic historical drama (The Lehman Trilogy), intimate solo performances (Lackawanna Blues), and exuberant pop spectacle (SIX). Gender-swapped revivals (Company) share the stage with urgent new American plays (Pass Over, Clyde's), demonstrating Broadway's capacity for both reinvention and innovation.

Whether you're drawn to experimental theater, classic musicals, or powerful new voices, these 2021 productions continue to define what Broadway became after its darkest period—and many remain essential viewing for anyone seeking to understand contemporary American theater.

Leading our rankings is a grittier reimagining of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace this fresh take on the beloved musical, though the production remains divisive for some traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as one of 2020's most significant theatrical events—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally receives its long-overdue Broadway premiere in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race, power, and identity remains urgently relevant.

The season also showcases notable experiments in form and interpretation. Laura Linney commands the stage in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, a solo adaptation that divides critics between those captivated by her luminous performance and those who question the theatrical translation of Elizabeth Strout's intimate novel. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining provokes strong reactions with its bold visual approach and contemporary staging choices.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the 2020 Broadway play season—though brief—delivered both thoughtful revivals and daring reinterpretations. Whether you're drawn to powerful dramas, intimate character studies, or bold directorial visions, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience what made it to the stage before everything changed.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the 2021 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period of renewal and artistic ambition. Following the industry's pandemic shutdown, these productions didn't simply reopen theaters—they redefined what Broadway could be.

The season's highest-rated show, **Dana H.**, demonstrates this adventurous spirit with its unconventional approach to storytelling. Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real-life interview transforms documentary material into gripping theater. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** delivers epic scope through intimate staging, tracing 160 years of American capitalism with extraordinary performances and stunning direction. Not all innovation requires experimental form: **Lackawanna Blues** proves that traditional solo performance can still captivate audiences when executed with Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic skill.

The season balances groundbreaking work with reimagined classics. Rebecca Frecknall's **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** transforms the Playhouse Theatre into an immersive Weimar-era nightclub, while Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** brings fresh perspective to Sondheim's masterwork. Even **The Phantom of the Opera**, critics acknowledge, continues to deliver spectacular entertainment despite—or perhaps because of—its unabashed theatricality.

With an impressive average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 season showcases Broadway at a creative peak, featuring everything from verbatim FBI transcripts (**Is This a Room**) to pop-concert reimaginings of Tudor history (**SIX**). Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama or crowd-pleasing spectacle, this collection represents the diverse range of theatrical excellence that marked Broadway's triumphant return.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both daring new voices and celebrated revivals to the stage. The shows that opened during this period continue to resonate with audiences, offering a diverse range of theatrical experiences from intimate character studies to sweeping historical dramas.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics hail as a near-perfect achievement, masterfully balancing comedy with genuine emotional depth. Close behind are two equally impressive productions: **Into the Woods**, a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as a powerful tribute to the late composer, and **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical that breaks new ground with its brazenly original storytelling.

The 2022 season proved particularly strong for Pulitzer Prize winners, with multiple award-winning plays making their Broadway debuts or returning in acclaimed revivals. **Topdog/Underdog** brought Suzan-Lori Parks' explosive drama back to life with electrifying performances, while Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt** offered audiences a haunting meditation on Jewish identity and the Holocaust. The year also showcased remarkable range, from Mike Birbiglia's solo performance exploring mortality to Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'**.

With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season demonstrated Broadway's capacity for both artistic excellence and meaningful storytelling. Whether you're drawn to innovative musicals, powerful dramas, or thought-provoking solo performances, these shows represent some of the finest theatrical work of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the 2023 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period for serious drama and theatrical innovation, with several productions proving their enduring power through extended runs and continued critical conversation.

The season's crown jewel is **Merrily We Roll Along**, Maria Friedman's revelatory revival that finally unlocked the emotional core of Sondheim's famously troubled 1981 musical. Critics uniformly praised the production for its intimate staging and deeply resonant performances, transforming what was once considered a noble failure into a triumph. Meanwhile, **Appropriate** emerged as a modern classic, with Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama earning near-universal acclaim for its unflinching examination of inherited racism and family dysfunction, anchored by Sarah Paulson's blistering performance.

The year also brought important revivals that resonated with contemporary audiences. **Purlie Victorious** proved that Ossie Davis's 1961 satire had lost none of its bite, while **Parade** found urgent new relevance in its story of injustice and antisemitism. More experimental voices found success as well, from James Ijames's Pulitzer-winning **Fat Ham**—a raucous Hamlet adaptation set at a Southern barbecue—to **Stereophonic**, an immersive rock studio drama that critics hailed as near-perfect theatrical craftsmanship.

With an average critical score of 82/100 across these ten productions, the 2023 season demonstrated Broadway's continued commitment to substantive drama alongside its commercial offerings. Whether you're drawn to musical revivals, contemporary social commentary, or innovative adaptations of classic stories, this collection represents some of the finest theatrical work of the decade—many still running or returning for limited engagements worth catching while you can.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As we look back from March 2026, the 2024 Broadway season stands out as a remarkably diverse and critically acclaimed period for theater, with shows that opened that year continuing to resonate with audiences today.

Leading the pack is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio, which critics consistently hail as a theatrical marvel for its authentic depiction of the creative process. The production demonstrates that original plays exploring niche subjects can achieve both critical excellence and commercial success when executed with precision and artistry.

The season's range is evident in its other standout productions. **Cole Escola's Oh, Mary!** proves that irreverent comedy has a vital place on Broadway, with the absurdist farce about a boozy, cabaret-obsessed Mary Todd Lincoln earning raves for its riotous humor and bold reimagining of historical figures. Meanwhile, **Maybe Happy Ending** brings something entirely different to the stage—a charming robot love story that critics praise as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, notable for its emotional depth and inventive premise.

The ten featured productions average an impressive 83 out of 100 in critical scores, spanning genres from intimate dramas like **Mary Jane** to lavish revivals such as **Oliver!** and **Gypsy**. The season includes both grassroots sensations that earned West End transfers and ambitious new works tackling subjects from the suffrage movement to dance-musical hybrids.

Whether you're drawn to innovative storytelling, classic revivals with fresh perspectives, or bold comedic experiments, these 2024 productions offer a comprehensive view of contemporary Broadway at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As March 2026 arrives, the Broadway season continues to showcase the exceptional plays that opened throughout 2025, offering audiences a rich variety of dramatic experiences. This month's top-rated productions demonstrate the enduring power of both classic American drama and bold contemporary voices.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread critical acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. Arthur Miller's classic examination of moral responsibility proves remarkably resonant in van Hove's stripped-down staging, achieving the highest critical score among current plays.

The **25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** returns to Broadway for its 20th anniversary, with critics celebrating the revival as joyous and perfectly timed. The production's airtight writing and emotional depth remind audiences why this intimate musical-comedy became a beloved fixture in the first place.

Among new works, **Liberation** stands out as Wohl's ambitious feminist memory play, praised for its timeliness and superb performances despite some structural reservations. Meanwhile, Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** earns strong notices for its smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity, and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another characteristically sharp family drama with **Purpose**.

The season also features well-received revivals of **Ragtime**, bolstered by Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance, and the enchanting family offering **Paddington The Musical**, which wins over critics with its remarkably lifelike bear puppet.

With an average critical score of 84/100 across these ten productions, this selection represents some of the strongest dramatic work currently available on Broadway. Whether drawn to reimagined classics or provocative new voices, theatergoers will find compelling options throughout the spring season.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
